question.problem:
The joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ for the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ is given below.

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=3$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=0$ | $0.15$ | $0.2$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.4$ | $0.25$ |

If $\text{E}[X]=1.3$ and $\text{E}[Y]=1.9,$ calculate the covariance of $X$ and $Y.$
question.worked_solution:
The covariance of $X$ and $Y$ can be calculated using the formula

$$
\text{Cov}[X,Y]=\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y].
$$

We use the rule of the lazy statistician to find $\text{E}[XY]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[XY] & ={\sum }_{(x,y)\in S}xy\cdot f(x,y) \\  & =(0)(1)(0.15)+(0)(3)(0.2)+(2)(1)(0.4)+(2)(3)(0.25) \\  & =2.3.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the covariance formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =2.3-(1.3)(1.9) \\  & =-0.17.\end{aligned}
$$
